subject: ubuntu 18.04 - lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collapse with observed

messages.author: e156e83d5c4b4d2f
messages.subject: ubuntu 18.04 - lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collapse with observed
parts:
Hi all,

I'm using lavaan in a shiny app to run a cfa.  The app runs correctly in rstudio and when deployed on shinyapps.io, but I'm getting an error when I deploy on a server that is using ubuntu 18.4. 

In particular, when I run a cfa, I am getting the following error: "lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collapse with observed".  The code for this error message comes from here: https://rdrr.io/github/yrosseel/lavaan/src/R/xxx_lavaan.R.  The cfa runs correctly in rstudio on windows 10.

I do not understand why this would only happen on linux, and I'm wondering if anyone else has run into this error.  I am running R 4.0.0.

Melissa

Update: 

I just realized that I was running lavaan 0.6-5 on my computer.  I updated to lavaan 0.6-6 since that is what is on ubuntu, and I am now getting the same error.  This appears to be a bug in lavaan 0.6-6.  Downgrading to 0.6-5 resolved the issue.

messages.subject: Re: ubuntu 18.04 - lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collapse with observed
parts:
On 5/23/20 2:57 AM, Melissa Gordon Wolf wrote:
> In particular, when I run a cfa, I am getting the following error:
> "lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collapse with observed".  The
> code for this error message comes from here:

The error message is claiming that your model contains latent variables,
and the names of those latent variables also appear in your dataset
(which should not happen, as this would imply they are manifest).

Could you check if this is indeed the case?

If your dataset is called 'Data', what is the output of

names(Data)

And what are the names of your latent variables?

If there is any overlap, this triggers the error message (which is new
in 0.6-6).

Renaming your latent variables should fix the problem. If not, please
send me your dataset and R script so I can investigate why this is not
working properly.

Yves.
